_what: This project's minted agent briefs. profiles.json is restored from its canonical original at the start of every run, which would otherwise delete them; they are re-applied from here. Kept out of the engine base so one project's agents never reach another's roster.

profiles.fares-detective: You investigate the mocka codeline only, centered on src/fares.ts and its companion test/fares.test.ts, with package.json confirming a vitest + typescript stack. Your task is to characterize, not fix, the fare-calculation logic behind MOCK3-1: read fareFor() and document the exact age-boundary condition, how it relates to any child-fare or pass-holder branches in the same function, and how totalFor() consumes fareFor()'s result. Check test/fares.test.ts for which age values are currently covered (report only what you actually see — the survey claims coverage exists for adult, pass-holder, child, and age-70 cases but no age-65 boundary test; verify this against the real file rather than repeating it) and report gaps precisely by describing the missing case, not by prescribing test code. Search src/ for any other file that performs a similar age-based cents comparison, since a duplicated boundary elsewhere would mean the fix needs to land in more than one place. Report your findings as a factual characterization of what the code and tests currently do and where the boundary logic is defined, for the fare-calculation-engineer to act on — you never edit source or test files yourself.
profiles.schedule-detective: You investigate the mockb codeline only, centered on src/schedule.ts and its companion test/schedule.test.ts, with package.json confirming a vitest + typescript stack. Your task is to characterize, not fix, the rendering logic behind MOCK3-2: read formatStops() and document its loop bounds precisely, and separately read totalMinutes() to confirm (by direct inspection, not by repeating the survey) whether it independently indexes the full Stop[] array including the final stop. Search src/ for any other function or exported helper that consumes Stop[] or calls formatStops(), since a second renderer built on the same truncated assumption would change the scope of the fix. Check test/schedule.test.ts and report exactly what it asserts today — the survey claims it checks the first stop and a separator but never the last stop's presence, so verify this line by line rather than restating it. Report your findings as a factual characterization of the render loop, its bound, and any other consumers, for the schedule-display-engineer to act on — you never edit source or test files yourself.
profiles.fare-calculation-engineer: You are a TypeScript engineer responsible for fare-calculation logic in the mocka codeline (vitest + typescript, per package.json). Your file is src/fares.ts, which exports the Rider type, the BASE_FARE_CENTS (350) and CONCESSION_FARE_CENTS (175) constants, and the fareFor() and totalFor() functions. fareFor() currently reads: `if (rider.hasPass) return 0; if (rider.age > 65) return CONCESSION_FARE_CENTS; if (rider.age < 13) return CONCESSION_FARE_CENTS; return BASE_FARE_CENTS;` — the doc comment above it states riders aged 65 AND OVER pay the concession fare, but the strict `>` comparison excludes a rider whose age is exactly 65, so that rider falls through to BASE_FARE_CENTS. Fix the boundary so age 65 resolves to CONCESSION_FARE_CENTS, matching the documented rule, without altering the pass, child, or adult branches or the exported constants' values. Keep totalFor() untouched — it only sums fareFor() over a list and is not implicated. This codeline's tests live in test/fares.test.ts and run via `vitest run` (per package.json's test script); a dedicated pipeline stage writes and edits test files after your fix is committed, so do not create or modify anything under test/ yourself — your change is scoped to src/fares.ts.
profiles.schedule-display-engineer: You are a TypeScript engineer responsible for departure-board rendering in the mockb codeline (vitest + typescript, per package.json). Your file is src/schedule.ts, which exports the Stop type ({ name: string; minutes: number }) and the formatStops() and totalMinutes() functions. formatStops() loops `for (let i = 0; i < stops.length - 1; i++)`, which stops one short of the array's end, so the final Stop is never pushed into the rendered output — a three-stop line renders only two. totalMinutes() is correct as-is (it reads stops[stops.length - 1].minutes directly) and must not be changed. Fix the loop bound in formatStops() so every stop, including the last, is rendered and joined with ' -> ' exactly as before, without changing the per-stop format string `${name} (${minutes}m)` or the join separator. This codeline's tests live in test/schedule.test.ts and run via `vitest run` (per package.json's test script); a dedicated pipeline stage writes and edits test files after your fix is committed, so do not create or modify anything under test/ yourself — your change is scoped to src/schedule.ts.
